core_sets.notes: The plain and header-encrypted base sets, the stored multi-volume sets and the RAR4 solid multi-member LZ set. rar stamps times into the headers and -hp draws a fresh KDF salt and IV per run.

edge_cases.notes: The edge-case sets (multi-file, directories, empty members, unicode names, recovery records, comments, both tiny-volume sets, best compression, long names, symlink) and the originals/ inputs the sibling recipes read.

encrypted.notes: The four -p sets per format: file data encrypted, headers readable. Every run draws a fresh KDF salt and IV.

generated_matrix.notes: The eight-way multi-volume matrix: two formats x two modes x plain and encrypted, over one pinned-encoder clip split into seven volumes.

heavy_damage.notes: The ~80 MB RAR5 archive with a 64 KiB-slice PAR2 set carrying 500 recovery blocks. Also imported by bench/rarpar-bench/config/corpus.json under a pinned digest (par2-heavy-damage-28 / -250).

inputs.notes: Writes the two binary inputs the rest of the corpus is built from. originals/binary.bin is a pure arithmetic ramp and is byte-reproducible; originals/test_clip.mkv comes from the pinned FFmpeg encoder in process.

large_sets.notes: The ~85 MB video-member sets that were imported from the Scryer e2e release gate before they had a recipe: the solid archives, the header-encrypted pair, the solid encrypted set, the CJK-named set and the three nested RAR-in-RAR chains; plus the deterministic RAR5 solid wrap-match regression fixture.

par2_captures.notes: Replays five par2cmdline-turbo shell tests that build their working directory at run time (they invoke the par2 binary, and one drew from /dev/urandom - this recipe uses a fixed deterministic blob instead) and captures the result as a deterministic tarball. The upstream data tarballs they start from are byte-identical imports in the same directory.

ppmd_perf.notes: Deterministic RAR4 order-16 PPMd performance corpus and the classic-volume (.rar/.r00/.r01/.r02) set. The payload is built in Python and handed to the pinned RAR 6.24 image, which writes both archives; `--all` writes them at their ledger paths.

ppmd_solid.notes: The two RAR4 PPMd correctness fixtures (sub-allocator restart, solid member boundary). Their payloads are deterministic; the archives are not, because rar stamps times into the headers. Both are also imported by bench/rarpar-bench/config/corpus.json under a pinned digest - see `xtask test-corpus bench-pins`.

real_world.notes: The PAR2 repair fixtures: one plain RAR5 LZ set and one encrypted RAR4 stored set, each with a PAR2 recovery set over its volumes.

recovery_volumes.notes: `rar a . -rv2` writes the data volumes and two .rev recovery volumes in one pass. The .rev format follows the archive format: RAR 2.9-format archives get RAR 3.x-style recovery volumes with no signature and a footer, RAR5 archives get signed RAR5 ones. RARLAB's writer produces the .rev files exactly as it produces the .rar ones.

stored_layout.notes: The stored-layout sets: a chain longer than twenty volumes, a recovery record on every volume, the -htb BLAKE2 switch, and the encrypted/plain/solid member pairs whose second member starts past the first volume.

junrar.notes: v8.1.0. junrar's LICENSE is the RARLAB 'UnRAR - free portable version' text (its POM declares 'UnRar License'); it is not Apache-2.0. The RAR 1.5 / 2.0 oracle archives and their expected WAV are immutable imports and are never assigned a RARLAB writer.

libarchive.notes: v3.8.9. Test archives live at libarchive/test/<name>.uu and are uudecoded before comparison; every local basename equals the upstream basename.

par2cmdline-turbo.notes: v1.4.0, the release the toolchain lock pins as the PAR2 generator. tests/*.tar.gz are byte-identical (and also identical in Parchive/par2cmdline v1.3.0).
